description: Single-panel double-logarithmic plot (no sub-panels) with lnσ (natural log of stress) on the ordinate, ticked at 6.0, 6.5, 7.0 and 7.5, and lnε (natural log of strain) on the abscissa, ticked at -5, -4, -3, -2 and -1. The legend distinguishes three tensile temperatures: -196 °C (blue triangles), -77 °C (red circles) and RT (grey squares). Each data series is fitted by two straight-line segments meeting at a knee; the lower-strain segment is annotated n1 and the higher-strain segment n2. The printed values are n1 = 0.204 and n2 = 0.448 for -196 °C, n1 = 0.181 and n2 = 0.439 for -77 °C, and n1 = 0.174 and n2 = 0.362 for RT. The RT data lie lowest (lnσ ≈ 5.9-6.9), the -77 °C data above them, and the -196 °C data highest (lnσ ≈ 6.8-7.6), so lowering the test temperature raises lnσ at a given lnε. Both stage slopes are largest at the lowest temperature, and n2 > n1 at every temperature. The figure therefore demonstrates a two-stage work-hardening response whose exponents increase as the tensile temperature decreases.
measured_quantities: lnσ (natural log of stress, dimensionless axis)
lnε (natural log of strain, dimensionless axis)
work hardening exponent n1 (low strain region, slope)
work hardening exponent n2 (high strain region, slope)

observations.observation: The plot shows lnσ on the y-axis (labelled ticks 6.0, 6.5, 7.0, 7.5) against lnε on the x-axis (labelled ticks -5, -4, -3, -2, -1).
Three data series are plotted and identified in the legend as -196 °C (blue triangles), -77 °C (red circles) and RT (grey squares).
The -196 °C series carries the printed annotations n1 = 0.204 and n2 = 0.448.
The -77 °C series carries the printed annotations n1 = 0.181 and n2 = 0.439.
The RT series carries the printed annotations n1 = 0.174 and n2 = 0.362.
Every series is fitted by two straight-line segments with a change of slope (knee), the first annotated n1 and the second n2, so n2 > n1 for all three temperatures.
At a given lnε the -196 °C data lie above the -77 °C data, which lie above the RT data (RT spans lnσ ≈ 5.9-6.9, -196 °C spans lnσ ≈ 6.8-7.6).
The caption states the figure is the 'Determination of work hardening exponent at different temperature'.
The citing text states that n1 is the slope in the low strain region and n2 the slope in the high strain region.
The citing text states that the work hardening exponent n1 increases with decreasing temperature, consistent with the printed n1 values 0.174 (RT) < 0.181 (-77 °C) < 0.204 (-196 °C).

The citing text states that at lower temperatures a higher n value indicates a more substantial strengthening effect from microbands, and that mechanical twins also contribute to improved work hardening at -196 °C.

subfigures.description: One lnσ vs lnε scatter plot with three series (-196 °C blue triangles, -77 °C red circles, RT grey squares), each fitted by two linear segments labelled n1 (low strain) and n2 (high strain) with printed slope values 0.204/0.448, 0.181/0.439 and 0.174/0.362 respectively. Axes: lnσ from 6.0 to 7.5, lnε from -5 to -1.
